verdict.rationale: Cal.com documents Cal.diy as an official, 100% MIT-licensed, self-hostable edition that runs without a license key or Cal.com account, and community users report self-hosting both the API and the database. However, Cal.diy is a fork with the enterprise code removed, so Teams, Organizations, Insights, Workflows and SSO are gone. Community reports also say its docs restrict it to personal, non-production use, public Docker images are being discontinued, and the Docker setup is hard to get working. missing for 10: a full-featured self-hostable edition of the core product, support for production or enterprise self-hosting, prebuilt Docker images, first-party self-hosting deployment docs.
